channel.title: The Daily Plant
channel.description: An automatically generated daily podcast for the serious gardener and designer. Each episode is a focused, master-gardener-level deep dive on a single plant or genus relevant to the Eastern US — native species, the non-native ornamentals and invasives you encounter in real gardens — covering identification, range and ecology, culture, mature habit, design use, companions, and the best cultivars. Most episodes end with a short spaced-repetition quiz on plants covered earlier, to build lasting recall.

item.title: The Daily Plant — Wild Roses (Rosa)
item.description:
A designer's tour of the genus Rosa on the East Coast: the native roses worth specifying (Virginia, Carolina, swamp, and climbing prairie rose), the invasive Asian roses you'll be ripping out (multiflora, rugosa on the dunes, Cherokee and Macartney in the South), and the rose rosette problem that ties them all together. item.title: The Daily Plant — Common Reed (Phragmites australis)
item.description:
An invasive-management episode on Phragmites australis, the tan-plumed reed now towering over every Eastern ditch, marsh edge, and stormwater basin. We cover the cryptic invasion story, how to tell the native subspecies from the Eurasian lineage in the field, why it wins, what it does and doesn't do ecologically, and a realistic fall control program for a designer inheriting a stand. Closes with a review quiz on Cotinus, Carpinus, Gentiana, and Fagus.

item.title: The Daily Plant — Beech (Fagus)

item.title: The Daily Plant — Red-osier Dogwood (Cornus sericea)
item.description:
A species deep dive on red-osier dogwood, Cornus sericea, the red-stemmed shrub dogwood that every Northeastern designer specifies and every Southern designer should think twice about. item.title: The Daily Plant — Boxwood (Buxus)
item.description:
A clear-eyed look at Buxus, the evergreen backbone of East Coast foundation plantings, now under pressure from two imported threats: boxwood blight and the box tree moth. We cover the species groups and the trade hybrids, blight-resistance data by cultivar, how the moth is spreading and how to manage it, culture and pruning that keep plants healthy, and when to specify an alternative. item.title: The Daily Plant — Callery Pear (Pyrus calleryana)
item.description:
An invasive-species deep dive on Callery pear, the tree behind 'Bradford', and why mid fall is the best time to map it. We cover the USDA fire blight program that brought it here, how self-incompatibility plus a crowd of cultivars turned a sterile clone into an invader, field ID against native look-alikes, the state bans and bounties now in force, control that actually works, and what to specify in its place.

item.title: The Daily Plant — Pachysandra (Allegheny spurge and Japanese pachysandra)
item.description:
A genus episode on Pachysandra, setting the native Allegheny spurge, Pachysandra procumbens, against the Japanese pachysandra that carpets half the foundation beds on the East Coast. Covers the genus's East Asia to eastern North America split, field identification, the surprisingly narrow native range, Volutella blight, invasive status and fall removal, the procumbens cultivars Silver Streak, Forest Green, Angola, and Pixie, and how to design with a clumping native instead of a monoculture. Closes with a six-question recall quiz on Boltonia, sassafras, smoketree, nandina, garden mums, and hornbeam.

A genus deep dive on Acer as the East Coast heads into peak fall color: the two workhorse natives, red maple and sugar maple, the floodplain also-ran silver maple and its Autumn Blaze hybrid, the invasive Norway maple you need to be able to name on sight, and the ubiquitous ornamental Japanese maple. item.title: The Daily Plant — Pawpaw (Asimina triloba)
item.description:
